topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the scope of the lecture on cancer causes, and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, environmental factors, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the origins of cancer by evaluating the relative contributions of intrinsic biological processes, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures through conceptual frameworks and epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens drive oncogenesis, illustrated in detail by the multifactorial etiology and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and xenobiotic metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and dietary or environmental chemicals induce DNA damage, focusing on metabolic activation, reactive epoxides, and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic factors in cancer development, including chronic inflammatory promoters, the initiator-promoter paradigm, and host developmental stage susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo models, and in vitro assays used to evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental carcinogenesis and reflections on everyday risk-benefit decision making.
